q4.sql:
-- Check if payment_value sums match order_items totals for multi-payment orders
SELECT op.order_id, SUM(op.payment_value) as total_payment, SUM(oi.price) + SUM(oi.freight_value) as total_order_cost
FROM order_payments op
JOIN order_items oi ON op.order_id = oi.order_id
GROUP BY op.order_id
HAVING COUNT(op.order_id) > 1
LIMIT 10

q5.sql:
-- Check if payment_value sums match order_items totals for single-payment orders
SELECT op.order_id, SUM(op.payment_value) as total_payment, SUM(oi.price) + SUM(oi.freight_value) as total_order_cost
FROM order_payments op
JOIN order_items oi ON op.order_id = oi.order_id
GROUP BY op.order_id
HAVING COUNT(op.order_id) = 1
LIMIT 10

-- Check how many orders have no payment record at all
SELECT COUNT(*) as orders_without_payment
FROM orders o
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_payments op WHERE op.order_id = o.order_id)

database_note: The orders table is the central hub for transactions, linking to customers via customer_id, to order_items via order_id, to order_payments via order_id, and to order_reviews via order_id. The order_items table connects to products via product_id and to sellers via seller_id. Use the products table for static product details and the sellers table for seller location information. The order_payments table records individual payment transactions for each order. The order_reviews table stores customer feedback for specific orders. The product_category_name_translation table provides English names for product categories found in the products table. The geolocation table contains geographic coordinates for zip code prefixes but does not directly join to other tables in this schema. The customers table holds customer identifiers and location data.
